message_capture.reason: All outbound protocol messages converge on a single choke point: node.emit (node.go:332-340) calls transport.Send. Transport is an injectable interface (Config.Transport, node.go:31,79) and the only implementation, MemoryTransport.Send, is the uncontrollable path because it synchronously calls the target's Step (transport.go:33-45). A NewMessageController can wrap this seam: capture a stable clone (Message.Clone, message.go:38-46) and suppress the underlying Send. There are no bypasses: heartbeats are just append messages through emit (node.go:117-122), there are no retries, snapshots, or forwarded requests (doc.go:5), and all handler outputs return through emit. No controller exists today, so the work is additive at an existing seam.
limitations: MessageController does not exist; constructor, ListPending, and ClearPending must be implemented.
MemoryTransport records delivered messages even after capture interception is added, so tests must not confuse transport.Delivered with controller pending state.
Capture suppresses only outbound protocol messages; a real network send path is outside the boundary and not implemented.
message_capture.suggested_direction: Implement NewMessageController(Transport) as a wrapper around the Transport interface: Send captures message.Clone() into a pending store with an incrementing CaptureSequence and returns without invoking the wrapped transport; ListPending returns stable metadata (ID, From, To, Type, CaptureSequence); ClearPending empties the store.

message_injection.boundary: protocol_library: delivery is through the in-memory Node.Step boundary; real networking is outside
message_injection.gap: No injection API or serialization between Inject/ClearPending and concurrent capture exists.
message_injection.reason: The normal protocol input boundary is Node.Step (node.go:133-146), which validates message.To against node.id, clones the message, processes it under the node mutex, and emits responses synchronously. A captured message records its target in To, so injection can deliver the exact pending message by calling the recorded node's Step. Sender, receiver, and content remain unchanged because pending messages are stable clones (message.go:38-46) and Step re-clones on entry (node.go:143). Processing is synchronous (Step completes under lock before returning). Failed injection (e.g., ErrPaused) can leave the message pending since Step returns an error without consuming the store. The controller must serialize Inject/ClearPending while capture may be concurrent.
limitations: Injection controller does not exist; Inject(messageID) and the pending-store identity (pending_store_instance or test_session) must be declared.
A captured message can only be injected into the node recorded in its To field; ErrWrongTarget (node.go:135) protects that invariant.
If the target node is paused at injection time, Step returns ErrPaused; the inject contract must keep the message pending in that case.
message_injection.suggested_direction: Add Inject(messageID) to the controller: look up the pending message by ID, call the recorded target's Step(pending.Message), and on success remove the message from the pending store; on error leave it pending. Serialize Inject and ClearPending with a mutex; allow capture (Send) to proceed concurrently.
entrypoints: Node.Step (node.go:134) - the original target node's normal protocol input boundary
